courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Art Lab
courses.description: An open lab for studio art students for the purpose of devoting additional hours outside of class time on projects. Projects, determined by class assignments, vary by semester. Twenty-seven lab hours per semester earn 0.5 unit. May be repeated. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. Open Entry/Open Exit. A combination of ART 130 and ART 148 and ART 230 and ART 233 and ART 248 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments.
review: Special accounting or noncredit course: scheduler must determine accounting method

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Mural Art Lab
courses.description: A lab for mural students to enhance skills and techniques on mural projects. Projects, determined by class assignments, vary by semester. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only.
review: Variable curriculum: selected units and component hours require verification

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to Art Concepts
courses.description: A study of the visual arts in relation to both personal and cultural expressions. Fundamentals of visual organization, color theory, terminology, historical art movements and concepts will be studied. Required for art majors. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Honors Introduction to Art Concepts
courses.description: Enriched exposure to a study of the visual arts in relation to personal and cultural expression with an emphasis on critical thinking and writing. Fundamentals of visual organization, color theory, terminology, historical art movements and concepts will be studied in a seminar format. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Arts of Africa, Oceania, and Indigenous North America
courses.description: History and appreciation of the arts of Africa, Oceania, and indigenous North America. Examines the visual arts of these vast and varied cultures within socio-political, aesthetic, religious contexts and their impact on Western art in Europe and the Americas. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Mexican and Chicano Art History
courses.description: The history and appreciation of Mexican and Chicano art from the pre-Columbian to the present including the modern murals of Mexico and the United States. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: History of Modern Art
courses.description: History of painting, sculpture, architecture, prints, and applied arts from the late nineteenth century through the twentieth century. Covers the formal philosophic, spiritual, and historical background of art from Post Impressionism to Post Modernism. For general students and art majors. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Asian Art History
courses.description: Historical survey of the visual arts of India, China, Japan, India, Korea and Southeast Asia. Includes relationship of Far Eastern philosophy and culture to artistic achievement. Emphasizes works of art in terms of style, technique, and content. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Contemporary Art History: Art Since Mid-Twentieth Century
courses.description: A survey course exploring post World War II styles, trends, ideas, and innovations in architecture and the visual arts in Europe and North America with references to globalization. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to Woodworking
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamentals of woodworking with a focus on wood as a medium for creative expression. Emphasizes knowledge of and proficiency with hard to soft woods; grain patterns; finishing techniques; fabrication; and joinery. Students learn and observe safety standards as they gain skills with hand tools, small power tools and larger machinery in the shop. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Two-Dimensional Design
courses.description: Introduction to the principles and elements of two-dimensional design. Provides instruction in the fundamentals of visual communication including color theory, composition, and expression. Application of concepts through creative projects. Required for art majors. A combination of Art 110 and 111 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Three-Dimensional Design
courses.description: An introduction to the fundamental concepts and technical processes of three-dimensional design. Coursework will focus on the formal development and articulation of three dimensional objects with an emphasis on form, mass, scale, texture, space, color, contrast and movement. A combination of Art 110 and 111 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Drawing for Non-Art Majors
courses.description: This is an introductory drawing class intended for students with little or no drawing experience and/or currently not majoring in art. Students will gain a greater appreciation of the history drawing and the art making process. The student will learn from a hands-on approach to basic observational drawing and composition. Students will learn about and employ the basic elements and principles of art, problem solving skills related to art making, how to use various basic drawing media, and become familiar with the basic vocabulary, concepts, and techniques of observational drawing. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership
No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to Drawing
courses.description: Introductory course in observational drawing, exploring line, form, proportion, composition, and a variety of media. Drawing from man-made and natural objects. Required for art majors. A combination of Art 130, 230, 233, and 250 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Beginning Life Drawing
courses.description: Introduction to drawing the human form by observing live models for studies in anatomy, structure, and composition. Students are both taught traditional and contemporary figurative drawing techniques, while exploring different media and methods. Required for art majors. A combination of Art 131, 231, 232, and 243 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Beginning Pastel Drawing and Painting
courses.description: Development of pastel drawing and painting skills using various techniques. Strong emphasis on color theory, value, and composition. Preparation of grounds using various papers. Study of historical and contemporary pastel styles and techniques. A combination of Art 132A and 132B may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Intermediate Pastel Drawing and Painting
courses.description: Intensive exploration of contemporary uses of pastels. Intermediate and advanced projects emphasizing pastel drawing/painting concepts in conjunction with other media. Emphasis on creative, personal expression, content, and style development. A combination of Art 132A and 132B may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to Gallery Production
courses.description: Introduction to the practices of art exhibit preparation and installation. Students will gain knowledge in the history and theory of art exhibition, as well as the current state of gallery management and museum work. Emphasis is on learning and utilizing industry-standard terminology, materials and tools. Students will move from observation to practical experience as they support the daily operations and special events of two college galleries. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. A combination of Art 133, 134, and 135 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Intermediate Gallery Production
courses.description: An intermediate course designed to build on knowledge and skills gained in Art 133. Students have opportunities to increase experience with new exhibitions and installations. Emphasis is on solving art gallery problems using current industry-standard communication and practices. Visits to local galleries and behind-the-scenes museum tours of collections and exhibition preparation areas. Students will also use woodshop equipment to build pedestals as well as draft an exhibition proposal and artwork layout. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. A combination of Art 133, 134, and 135 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Advanced Gallery Production
courses.description: Students produce a unique exhibition on campus using knowledge and skills gained in Art 133 and 134. Emphasis will be on independently curating, designing, lighting, writing didactic material, and publicizing their exhibition. Grade: Pass/No Pass Only. A combination of Art 133, 134, and 135 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Watercolor Painting
courses.description: Introduction to watercolor painting as a creative art form with emphasis on transparent watercolor techniques. Course includes principles of composition and color theory, materials selection, tools, terminology, and various watercolor techniques. Students develop basic watercolor skills while painting from simple forms and progressing to a variety of subjects. A combination of Art 140A, 140B, 143, and 240 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Watercolor Painting
courses.description: A continuing course in transparent watercolor techniques providing the opportunity to advance the creativity of those with basic skills in watercolor. Further study of formal elements and composition while painting from varied subject matter. Emphasis on refinement of methods and techniques for more expressive painting. A combination of Art 140A, 140B, 143, and 240 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Beginning Painting
courses.description: Introduction to acrylic and/or water soluble oil painting as a creative art form with exposure to historical, traditional and contemporary painting styles. Course includes principles of composition and color theory, materials selection, tools, terminology, and techniques. Students develop basic skills painting a variety of subjects. Required for art majors. A combination of Art 141, 241, and 242 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Landscape Watercolor
courses.description: Intermediate course in transparent watercolor using the Southern California landscape as studio and subject for paintings. Explores a variety of techniques, papers, brushes, and pigments. Further study of compositional/conceptual elements leading to development of individual expression. A combination of Art 140A, 140B, 143, and 240 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to Illustration
courses.description: Introduction to the illustrative arts with an emphasis on traditional handmade process. Editorial illustration, technical illustration, book illustration, and fashion Illustration are introduced. Focus is on developing technical and conceptual expertise. This course examines master works by historically significant and contemporary illustrators, fine-art painters and other commercial artists. A combination of ART 130 and ART 148 and ART 230 and ART 233 and ART 248 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Primitive Pottery Techniques
courses.description: Primitive techniques in pottery construction and firing. Emphasizes handbuilt forms. Students will construct tools. Sawdust, raku, dung, low temperature salt, and other pit firings will be utilized. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramics-Introductory Level
courses.description: Exploration of clay as a structural and creative material. Experiences include throwing on the potter's wheel and hand building. Instruction includes surface design, glazing, and experience in utilitarian forms. Students provide clay and tools. A combination of Art 151, 152, and 153 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramics-Intermediate Throwing
courses.description: Further study of wheel thrown techniques with an emphasis on functional, utilitarian forms. Students provide own clay and tools. A combination of Art 151, 152, and 153 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramics-Intermediate Handbuilding
courses.description: Further study of handbuilding techniques with emphasis on one-of-a-kind sculptural forms. Non-traditional alternatives to glazes are explored. Students provide own clay and tools. A combination of Art 151, 152, and 153 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramics Summer Workshop
courses.description: For intermediate/advanced students interested in a self-guided study/exploration in the ceramic medium. Emphasizes technical aspects and artistic imageries. Invited artists will provide supplementary guidance. Students provide own clay and tools. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Plaster Mold Making
courses.description: Basic aspects of plaster of Paris mold making: production of molds from original models in order to reproduce those models; alteration of those plaster mold castings into a more artistic, personalized imagery. A combination of Art 155 and 157 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Clay Calculation: An Approach in Color Study
courses.description: Basic uses of color clays as a decorative tool in making pottery forms. Techniques of sprigging, incising, inlay, and lamination are utilized with wheel-thrown, handbuilding, and plaster mold construction methods. A combination of Art 156, 159A, and 159B may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramics-Raku and Saggar Firing Techniques
courses.description: Use of the potter's wheel and/or handbuilding techniques as methods for constructing vessel forms. Includes a study of surface coloration from natural organic materials. Several firing techniques will be utilized. A combination of Art 155 and 157 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramic Mural Project
courses.description: Students will work collaboratively to design, construct, and install tile murals. Students will learn various techniques of surface textures, painting, glaze colors, spatial compositions, and technical processes of installation. Students provide their own clay and tools. Projects vary each semester. A combination of ART 156 and ART 159B may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership
No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramic Color Decoration: High Temperature
courses.description: Exploration of surface color decoration on ceramic vessels within the realm of high stoneware temperatures. Emphasizes glazing techniques such as marbling, feathering, mishima, brush decoration, stencils, stamp printing, spraying, slip painting, glaze trailing, wax resist, and terra sigallata. A combination of Art 156, 159A, and 159B may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Digital Illustration I
courses.description: Explores the essentials of illustration for graphic designers and concept artists, using industry-standard production and design tools. Focuses on professional studio techniques to master this essential design tool for the creation of sophisticated graphics. Emphasizes efficient workflow, technical proficiency, and aesthetic judgment. Students produce portfolio-ready projects using a broad range of imaging skills. The primary software used includes Adobe Photoshop, supplemented with Adobe Illustrator, and some time-based media software. (Same as Digital Media 162). A combination of Art 162, 191A, 192A, and Digital Media 162, 191A, 192A may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Graphic Design II: Branding & Identity
courses.description: A comprehensive design course serving as the capstone for all Digital Media Arts & Graphic Design programs. Students develop a career/transfer-ready digital portfolio through team-based branding and identity design development for multiple media applications. Focus is on both business and personal branding. Career goals, resumes, online portfolios, interviewing skills, and customer service needs are addressed. 6 units of digital media-oriented coursework recommended. (Same as Digital Media 168). CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership
No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to Mural Painting and Design
courses.description: A directed field studies course in designing and painting large-scale public art murals. Students will work collaboratively in groups and with the community to create designs. This class explores the various processes involved in the construction of large-scale public art while painting a variety of subject matter. Students will learn about historical, traditional and contemporary mural painting styles. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership
No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Digital Illustration II: Advanced Topics
courses.description: Examines advanced design and illustration techniques using industry-standard software via Adobe Creative Cloud. Addresses contemporary illustrative problems, concepts, and skills development within the digital media and graphic arts industries for the creation of unique illustrations. The technical needs for graphic illustrations for print, animation, film, and the web will also be addressed. Primary Software: Adobe Illustrator, supplemented with Adobe Photoshop. (Same as Digital Media 192A). A combination of Art 191A, 192A, 162, and Digital Media 192A may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Introduction to Digital Media Arts
courses.description: Foundation-level course designed for graphic designers, artists, photographers, web designers, programmers, and animation artists working in the digital realm. Students are introduced to fundamental concepts, practices, and theories of digital art production. Course topics include integration of traditional design, color, and compositional principles with contemporary digital tools, including industry-standard software, such as Adobe Creative Cloud for print, web and time-based media. (Same as DM 195). CSU/UC

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Topics
courses.description: This course provides an introduction to a basic hands-on experience of compositing for special effects as used in television, film and electronic games. There will be an emphasis on how digital 3D elements can be incorporated into the composite and how 3D scenes can be enhanced with the use of compositing techniques. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership
No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Intermediate Drawing
courses.description: An intermediate course in the study of drawing designed to give students who have completed an introductory drawing course additional opportunity in graphic expression. Further exploration of materials including a wide variety of both drawing and mixed media. Students continue the development of composition and more intermediate concepts. The class emphasizes individual expression. A combination of Art 130, 230, 233, and 250 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Intermediate Life Drawing
courses.description: Continued experience in figure drawing from the live model, with an opportunity for development of self-expression. Further exploration of media and techniques. A combination of Art 131, 231, 232, and 243 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Advanced Life Drawing
courses.description: Intensive study of drawing the human figure with further advanced level development of drawing skills, composition, technique, and media utilizing the live model. Projects vary each semester. A combination of Art 131, 231, 232, and 243 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Advanced Drawing
courses.description: To further develop individual expression and advanced skill sets in drawing. Students will plan a series of drawing problems to be executed during the semester under the instructor's direction. Exploration of new materials and techniques. A combination of Art 130, 230, and 233 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Anatomical Drawing
courses.description: In this course students will learn about realistic (artistic) representation of the human skeletal structure and musculature system with emphasis on function and relationship within the human figure. This course will explain and demonstrate specific areas of the human body, by breaking the figure down into manageable components and learning to draw them realistically from multiple aspects. Student's will work from, Anatomical Studies, Skeletons, Plaster casts and the occasional Figure Model. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership
No section offering on record in CU0321; planning signal only - verify before scheduling

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Intermediate Watercolor
courses.description: An intermediate level course providing for continuing development of watercolor painting skills. Further refinement of media, technique and expression of style through more advanced painting projects. Subject matter content includes still life, landscape, figurative studies, abstraction, and individual creative expression. Traditional and non-traditional approaches. A combination of Art 140A, 140B, 143, and 240 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Intermediate Painting
courses.description: An intermediate level class designed to promote and advance the creative development of those with basic skills in water-soluble oil and/or acrylic painting. Opportunity for further study of historical and contemporary references and to increase experience with new media, methods, and techniques. Emphasis on artistic expression and individual creative problems. A combination of Art 141, 241, and 242 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Advanced Painting
courses.description: An advanced level studio course providing opportunity for further refinement of painting skills with increasing exposure to contemporary styles. Emphasis on research and individual creative problems in painting. Exploration into a personal mode of expression through development of media, technique, and style. Classroom studio use of oils limited to water-soluble oil paint only. A combination of Art 141, 241, and 242 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Portrait and Life Painting
courses.description: Painting of the human form with study of portraiture and anatomy. Compositions in representation of the life model through interpretive studies in watercolor, pastels, water soluble oil, and acrylic. Study of traditional and contemporary methods and directions. A combination of Art 131, 231, 232, and 243 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Intermediate Illustration
courses.description: This course will explore the further development of conceptual and technical expertise in the field of Illustrative arts. This class will focus on book illustration, technical rendering/ illustration, bio-medical illustration, and editorial illustration. The course examines master works by contemporary and historic artists. Emphasis on developing individual creative style. A combination of ART 130 and ART 148 and ART 230 and ART 233 and ART 248 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramics-Advanced Throwing and Handbuilding
courses.description: Study of thrown and handbuilt sculptural forms. Exploration of decoration and glaze techniques and incorporation of non-traditional materials such as metal/wood/plastics/paints. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Ceramics-Advanced Study Process in Ceramics With Non-Traditional Media
courses.description: An advanced study in the ceramic process as it relates to a non-clay media approach. A sculptural form study with non-traditional materials as surface enhancements. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Electric Kiln Ceramics
courses.description: Provides student potters working studio production knowledge of the uses of an oxidizing electric kiln. Emphasizes types of electric kilns, spectrum of glaze formulas, and safety procedures of firing. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Mural Painting and Design II
courses.description: An intermediate level mural art class designed to promote and advance the creative development of those with basic skills in mural painting. Opportunity for further study of historical and contemporary references and to increase experience with new media, methods, and techniques. Students will work collaboratively in groups and with the community to create designs. Intermediate students will take on more leadership roles in the group creative dynamic. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Mural Painting and Design III
courses.description: An advanced level studio course providing opportunity for further refinement of large scale painting skills with increasing exposure to contemporary styles in mural painting. Exploration into an advanced personal mode of expression through development of media, technique, and style. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: ART
courses.title: Professional Art Production
courses.description: Designed to provide practice in developing digital 3D or multimedia art projects for actual clients or in a simulated setting. Students choose an art project based on strengths, interests and market need to work on during the class. CSU
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: DM
courses.title: 3D Character Animation
courses.description: From Star Trek to Wall-E, 3D characters are unique vessels supporting contemporary and creative narratives! In this course we offer instruction in the theories and practice of character animation. We address strategies for rigging, skinning and animating using character design. You will develop a short, animated narrative with a team of your peers and improve your creative portfolio. A combination of Art 165, 167, 184, 185 and Digital Media 165 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

chairOptions.label: In person / face-to-face
chairOptions.description: Meets on campus at scheduled days/times.

chairOptions.label: Fully online (asynchronous)
chairOptions.description: Fully Online Instruction. Students are required to log in to Canvas by the first day of class for detailed information and required course work. https://canvas.sac.edu There will be no instructional meetings.

chairOptions.label: Fully online live (Zoom)
chairOptions.description: Fully Online Live Instruction.  Live streaming instruction via Zoom during the days and times indicated. Students log in to Canvas. https://canvas.sac.edu.  There will be no instruction on-campus.

chairOptions.label: On-campus hybrid
chairOptions.description: On-Campus Hybrid Instruction. A combination of on-campus meetings during the days and times indicated and online instruction. Students log in to Canvas. https://canvas.sac.edu

chairOptions.label: Virtual hybrid

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
